Fire and River

Borrow Fire, Then Become Fire

Borrow the fire of intelligence; through practice, develop understanding, judgment, creation, and the capacity to keep becoming.

The argument moves from acquiring capability to cultivating a person, through finite inquiry, cooperation, and realization, then into lived feedback and shared creation. Capacities can be internalized or reliably distributed across person, models, and tools. Yinyang is one developed philosophical and working form within it.

01

Starting point: borrowed fire and the becoming of agents

Preview the argument, establish value and agency, give cultivation its conditional rationale through super-cuteness, then embody that direction in Baby Heraclitus.

02

Understanding: finite inquiry in a changing world

Make understanding corrigible: move from representation and time into reasoning, connect conflict, view selection, and support through the preference harness, then examine finite abstraction.

03

Encounter: making shared participation possible

Develop the agent concept into reciprocal generation and actual participation, preserving human initiative and model contributions.

04

Formation: from human agency to personal philosophy and practice

Human agency is the starting point: an existing agent draws on generative capabilities to develop a personal philosophy, worldview, and sustainable form of living.

05

Practice: becoming fire through environment and feedback

Begin your own practice, then enter its three environmental forms, experimental feedback, and further creation with others.

Begin your own practice

Begin with the getting-started guide and ask a model to help form and realize your arrangement. Return to conceptual reading by question; completing the series is not a prerequisite.
